title: What's New: Python 3.8 → 3.14
html:
The features added in each recent release — what interviewers mean by “modern Python”, and what you'll see in current codebases.

Release cadence

A new Python 3.x ships every October and gets ~5 years of support. At the time of writing 3.14 is current and 3.9 and older are end-of-life. Check yours with python3 --version or sys.version_info.

At a glance

VersionHeadline features
3.8 (2019)Walrus :=, positional-only params /, f"{x=}", functools.cached_property, math.prod / isqrt
3.9 (2020)Dict merge | / |=, str.removeprefix / removesuffix, list[int] generics without typing, zoneinfo
3.10 (2021)match statement, X | Y union types, zip(strict=True), parenthesised with, much better error messages
3.11 (2022)10–60% faster CPython, ExceptionGroup / except*, add_note, tomllib, asyncio.TaskGroup, typing.Self, error locations with ^^^
3.12 (2023)Type-parameter syntax def f[T], type alias statement, f-strings may reuse quotes and nest freely, itertools.batched, @override
3.13 (2024)New colourful REPL, experimental free-threaded build (no GIL) and JIT, copy.replace, removed old “dead battery” modules
3.14 (2025)Deferred evaluation of annotations, template strings t"…", free-threading officially supported, except A, B without brackets, concurrent.interpreters, compression.zstd

3.8 – 3.9: walrus, /, = debugging, dict union

3.10: match, X | Y, strict zip

3.11: speed, exception groups, notes

3.11 was the first release of the Faster CPython project — an adaptive, specialising interpreter that made typical code 10–60% faster with no changes. It also made concurrent failures first-class.

3.12: generics syntax & f-string freedom

3.13: new REPL, free-threading, JIT

New interactive shell

Colour, multi-line editing, history browsing, and exit / help work without parentheses.

Free-threaded build

An optional python3.13t build without the GIL, so threads can run Python code on several cores. Experimental in 3.13.

Experimental JIT

A copy-and-patch JIT compiler, off by default — groundwork for future speed-ups.

copy.replace()

One function to make a modified copy of dataclasses, named tuples, datetimes and more.

3.14: t-strings, lazy annotations, except A, B

Template strings look like f-strings but produce a Template object instead of a str, so a library can see the static text and the interpolated values separately — the safe way to build SQL, HTML or shell commands.

Also in 3.14What it gives you
Free-threaded build supportedpython3.14t is no longer experimental (still optional; the default build keeps the GIL)
concurrent.interpretersSeveral isolated interpreters in one process — parallelism without separate processes
compression.zstdZstandard compression in the standard library
finally warningsreturn / break / continue inside finally now warns — it silently swallows exceptions
Better errorsSuggestions for mistyped keywords (whille → while?)
Watch out

When a job description or codebase pins an older version, avoid the newer syntax: match needs 3.10, except* 3.11, def f[T] 3.12, t-strings 3.14. Check requires-python in pyproject.toml.

Name three features added to Python in the last few versions.

For example: structural pattern matching (match, 3.10), exception groups with except* and the big interpreter speed-up (3.11), the def f[T] generics syntax (3.12), the optional no-GIL free-threaded build (3.13, supported in 3.14), and template strings t"…" (3.14).

What is the difference between an f-string and a t-string?

An f-string is evaluated immediately into a str. A t-string (3.14) evaluates the expressions but returns a Template holding the literal parts and the values separately, so code can escape or transform the values before producing the final string — useful for preventing injection in SQL, HTML and shell commands.
